content.title: 15.1 — Learning objective
content.content: Construct and solve simple equations with algebraic fractions.

content.title: 15.1 — Scope summary
content.content: Review simple equations with brackets, variables on both sides and fractional terms. Extend this work to equations with an unknown in the denominator and to constructing equations from problem situations.

content.title: 15.1 — Constructing the divisor equation
content.content: Represent the two divisors by x and 2x. Write their quotients as 12/x and 12/(2x), and express the given difference as an equation. Use equivalent fractions with a common denominator, then multiply both sides by that denominator to solve.

content.title: 15.1 — Two divisors of twelve (opening worked problem)
content.content: Twelve is divided by two numbers, one double the other; the quotients differ by 2. Let the numbers be x and 2x. Then 12/x - 12/(2x) = 2. Rewriting with denominator 2x gives 24/(2x) - 12/(2x) = 2, hence 12/(2x) = 2. Multiplying by 2x gives 12 = 4x, so x = 3. The two numbers are 3 and 6.

content.title: 15.2 — Elimination summary
content.content: Construct a pair of equations from the problem. When coefficients differ, multiply an equation to make the coefficients of one unknown equal. Subtract the equations to eliminate that unknown, then substitute the result into an original equation to find the other value.

content.title: 15.3 — Factorization and zero-product summary
content.content: A quadratic equation has the form ax² + bx + c = 0, with a ≠ 0. Factorize the expression and use the fact that a zero product has at least one zero factor. Solve the resulting simple equations and check the roots in the original equation.
